description.narrative:
EMERGENCY FOOD SECURITY AND VULNERABLE LIVELIHOODS
The Emergency food Security (FSVL) response includes different activities that will be identified depending on the situation, target groups and their needs. Shifting between modalities will also be considered, depending on the context and market changes.
a. Food Provision (In-kind Parcels to IDPs/host families) Euro 408,925 for 1,200HHs Food items will be distributed in the IDP camps and HHs hosting IDPs to reduce the burden of food shortage. The market assessment conducted by the Oxfam team will inform the frequency and quantity of distribution food required, according to the Food Safety and Standard (FSS) - based on Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs (MoHA) lists which Oxfam will verify. Women headed households hosting IDPs willbe prioritised.
b. Cash for Work for host families/IDPs Euro 75,000 for 120HHs This activity includes the distribution of cash vouchers to HHs, especially women headed households, who are displaced or in host families.This activity is essentially a Social Protection Programme in the 6 selected project Local Government Areas of Adamawa and Taraba states. It will focus on how HHs will be able to quickly earn cash under ‘decent work’ conditions to enable them to get backon their feet. The HHs will in return for participating in disaster clean up and restoration activities get cash to meet their immediate HHs needs. This will be for a three-week durationand based on the need for the communities. Vouchers will be used toreduce the risk of handling cash. A rapid assessment will be conducted to determine how functional the local markets will be because the system requires contracted shops that will include grocery items and some hygiene materials for purchase with the voucher.
Cash Transfer (CT) based on survival Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB) will be provided for 3 rounds (112.75 EUR * 3 payments) over 3 months for affected families, who have lost their homes, or that are severely damaged, and so giving access to basicneeds and services. Women headed households will be prioritized and Oxfam will coordinate with Cash Working Group (CWG) members using MoHA lists that have been verified.
c. Dry season farming support to HHs Euro 226,075 for 320HHs When the floods start receding, this will leave behind rich agricultural soils for dry season farming along riverbanks that can be used by farmers to cultivate staple foods. Technical know-how, awareness and capacity building will be shared with the landowners / farmers,on good agricultural practices. These households will be provided with seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides to produce food products common to their communities. Water pumps will be provided and boreholes drilled for groups of farmers to be able to access water for their dry season farming activities

participating-org.narrative: The Christian Rural and Urban Development Association of Nigeria(CRUDAN) is a Christian inter-denominational, not-for-profit, Non-Governmental Organization. It is a membership organization that has as its members-Churches, Christian organizations and individuals that are engaged or interested in development work in Nigeria. It has the main goal of promoting the growth of the church in Nigeriaby assisting in rural/urban development work that is part of her witness. CRUDAN serves the church all over Nigeria in Wholistic development work. CRUDAN was formed in 1990, following the merger of two Christian organizations that operated independently in the country, namely Christian Rural Advisory Council(CRAC), Founded in 1965 in the Northern part of Nigeria, and Christian Rural Fellowship of Nigeria(CRFN), established in 1953, in the Southern part of Nigeria. Being a membership organization, the members from the general assembly that elects the board. CRUDAN has five(5) zones within the country namely, Central,Northeast, Northwest, Southeast and Southwest zones with a Zonal facilitator and Administrative Assistant for each zone. With this arrangement, CRUDAN is able to effectively cover the whole nation. CRUDAN began operation in 1991 and was officially registered by the Corporate Affairs Commission(CAC) of the Federal Government of Nigeria on 7th December 1992. Registration number 7111.
